requirements.name: TLE Data Ingestion
requirements.description: Fetch and parse current TLE orbital elements from CelesTrak API (or alternative) for ~10,000 satellites, including satellite catalog metadata (e.g., NORAD ID, name, classification).

requirements.name: Orbital Propagation (SGP4/SGP8)
requirements.description: Propagate satellite orbits in real-time using the SGP4/SGP8 model (or higher-fidelity alternative) to compute positions every second, accounting for perturbations (e.g., drag, gravitational effects).

requirements.name: Coordinate Transformations
requirements.description: Convert propagated orbital positions from Earth-Centered Inertial (ECI) coordinates to Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed (ECEF) and then to geodetic coordinates (latitude, longitude, altitude) using WGS84 ellipsoid model.

requirements.name: 3D Globe Rendering (WebGL)
requirements.description: Render an interactive 3D globe in the browser using WebGL/Three.js, displaying satellite positions as markers with altitude indicators and ground tracks for selected satellites.

requirements.name: Ground Track Computation
requirements.description: Compute and visualize ground tracks (projected satellite paths on Earth's surface) for selected satellites, accounting for Earth's rotation and satellite motion.

requirements.name: Backend Framework (Python/TypeScript)
requirements.description: Develop backend services in Python (e.g., FastAPI, Django) or TypeScript (e.g., NestJS, Express) to handle TLE data fetching, orbital propagation, and coordinate transformations.

requirements.name: Real-Time Data Streaming
requirements.description: Stream propagated satellite positions to the frontend at 1Hz (or higher) with minimal latency, using WebSockets or Server-Sent Events (SSE).

requirements.name: Scalability for 10,000 Satellites
requirements.description: Optimize backend and frontend to handle real-time propagation and rendering for 10,000 satellites without excessive computational overhead (e.g., batch processing, WebAssembly acceleration).

requirements.name: WebAssembly (WASM) Acceleration
requirements.description: Offload computationally intensive tasks (e.g., SGP4 propagation, coordinate transformations) to WebAssembly for browser-based performance optimization.

requirements.name: Satellite Metadata Integration
requirements.description: Integrate satellite metadata (e.g., name, classification, owner) into the visualization for contextual information.

requirements.name: User Interaction
requirements.description: Support user interactions such as satellite selection, zoom/pan controls, and dynamic filtering of satellites (e.g., by type, altitude, or owner).

requirements.name: Error Handling and Fallbacks
requirements.description: Implement robust error handling for TLE data fetching, orbital propagation failures, and WebGL rendering issues, with fallback mechanisms (e.g., cached data, simplified visualization).

requirements.name: Performance Profiling
requirements.description: Profile and optimize critical paths (e.g., SGP4 propagation, coordinate transformations, WebGL rendering) to ensure smooth real-time performance.

requirements.name: Data Persistence
requirements.description: Optionally persist satellite data and ground tracks for offline use or historical analysis.

requirements.name: Alternative Orbital Models
requirements.description: Support higher-fidelity orbital models (e.g., SDP4, EGP4) for improved accuracy, especially for low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellites.

requirements.name: Vector Tile Generation Pipeline
requirements.description: Build a pipeline to convert OpenStreetMap data (OSM PBF) into vector tiles (e.g., MBTiles or MVT) for a country-scale region, supporting customizable styling and GeoJSON overlays.

requirements.name: Self-Hosted Vector Tile Storage
requirements.description: Store generated vector tiles as static files in object storage (e.g., S3, GCS, or MinIO) for low-latency, scalable, and cost-efficient delivery.

requirements.name: Browser-Compatible Rendering
requirements.description: Render vector tiles in the browser using a lightweight, customizable map library (e.g., MapLibre GL JS, Deck.gl, or Leaflet with vector tile plugins) with support for dynamic GeoJSON overlays.

requirements.name: Customizable Styling Engine
requirements.description: Implement or integrate a styling engine (e.g., MapLibre Style Specification, SLD, or custom JSON-based rules) to allow dynamic theming of vector tiles and GeoJSON overlays.

requirements.name: GeoJSON Overlay Support
requirements.description: Enable seamless integration of custom GeoJSON datasets as additional tile layers, with support for dynamic updates and styling alignment with vector tiles.

requirements.name: Monthly Data Updates
requirements.description: Automate the process of updating OSM data and regenerating vector tiles on a monthly cadence, with minimal downtime or disruption to the live map service.

requirements.name: Vendor-Free Cost Model
requirements.description: Eliminate per-request fees from third-party map vendors by fully self-hosting the entire pipeline (data ingestion, tile generation, storage, and rendering).

requirements.name: Performance Optimization for Static Tiles
requirements.description: Optimize tile generation and storage for static delivery (e.g., pre-computed tiles, efficient tile indexing, and compression) to minimize bandwidth and rendering latency.

requirements.name: Tile Cache Invalidation Strategy
requirements.description: Implement a cache invalidation mechanism for monthly updates to ensure users receive the latest tiles without excessive reprocessing or storage bloat.

requirements.name: Scalable Tile Generation Infrastructure
requirements.description: Design the pipeline to scale horizontally for large country-scale datasets (e.g., using distributed task queues like Celery or Kubernetes for tile generation).

requirements.name: GeoJSON Overlay Performance
requirements.description: Ensure GeoJSON overlays render efficiently in the browser, even for large datasets, by leveraging spatial indexing (e.g., R-tree) or server-side filtering.

requirements.name: API for Dynamic GeoJSON Updates
requirements.description: Provide a lightweight API endpoint to dynamically update GeoJSON overlays without regenerating the entire tile set (e.g., using a tile server like TileServer or MapProxy).

requirements.name: Tile Server for Dynamic Rendering
requirements.description: Deploy a tile server (e.g., MapServer, TileServer, or custom solution) to handle dynamic tile requests if static tiles alone are insufficient for custom overlays.

requirements.name: Data License Compliance
requirements.description: Ensure compliance with OpenStreetMap's data license (ODbL) and any custom GeoJSON dataset licenses when distributing or rendering the map.

requirements.name: Multi-Source Data Ingestion
requirements.description: Ingest data from **three REST APIs** (with rate limits, pagination, and authentication) and **CSV exports** (local/remote S3/HTTP). Support for incremental updates (e.g., last-modified timestamps, API versioning).

requirements.name: Retry & Fault Tolerance
requirements.description: Automatic retries for failed API calls/CSV downloads with exponential backoff. Dead-letter queue (DLQ) for permanently failed records with human review triggers.

requirements.name: Data Quality Checks (Blocking)
requirements.description: Embedded validation rules (e.g., **schema validation**, **referential integrity**, **range checks**, **null/duplicate detection**) that **block pipeline progression** if failures exceed thresholds. Support for custom SQL/rule-based checks.

requirements.name: Data Lineage & Provenance
requirements.description: Track **source-to-target** lineage (e.g., API endpoint → table column) with timestamps, transformation steps, and failure reasons. Exportable as JSON/CSV for auditing.

requirements.name: PostgreSQL Target Integration
requirements.description: Efficient bulk inserts/updates into PostgreSQL with **transactional integrity** (ACID compliance). Support for **schema evolution** (e.g., adding columns without breaking pipelines).

requirements.name: Transformation Logic
requirements.description: SQL-based transformations (e.g., joins, aggregations) or **lightweight Python/R** for complex logic. Ensure transformations are **idempotent** and **deterministic** for reprocessing.

requirements.name: Alerting & Notifications
requirements.description: Real-time alerts (Slack/Email) for pipeline failures, data quality issues, or critical thresholds (e.g., >10% bad records). Support for escalation policies.

requirements.name: Performance Optimization
requirements.description: Parallelize independent data sources/transformations. Use **batch processing** (e.g., 10K rows at a time) to minimize PostgreSQL load. Cache API responses where possible.

requirements.name: Monitoring & Observability
requirements.description: Metrics (e.g., execution time, record counts, error rates) via **Prometheus/Grafana** or custom dashboard. Logs with structured JSON for debugging.

requirements.name: Idempotent Reprocessing
requirements.description: Support for reprocessing failed batches without duplicate data or overwrites. Use **merge strategies** (e.g., `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`) in PostgreSQL.

requirements.name: Data Governance & Access Control
requirements.description: Role-based access control (RBAC) for pipeline execution (e.g., admins vs. analysts). Audit logs for who triggered reprocessing.

requirements.name: API Rate Limit Handling
requirements.description: Dynamic throttling to avoid API rate limits (e.g., burst requests + delays). Cache responses with **TTL-based invalidation**.

requirements.name: Data Masking for Sensitive Fields
requirements.description: Automatically mask PII (e.g., SSNs, emails) in staging tables before reporting exposure. Support for dynamic masking rules.

requirements.name: Manual Job Retry Functionality

requirements.name: Redis Integration for Job Storage

requirements.name: PostgreSQL for Job Metadata and Persistence

requirements.name: Cross-Language Job Processing
requirements.description: Ensure the job system supports both Node.js (e.g., using `bull`, `agenda`, or custom solution) and Python (e.g., `celery`, `rq`, or custom solution) workers seamlessly.

requirements.name: Job State Management
requirements.description: Implement robust job state management (e.g., `pending`, `running`, `failed`, `completed`, `delayed`) with atomic updates to avoid race conditions.

requirements.name: Scalability for High Throughput

requirements.name: Monitoring and Alerts
requirements.description: Integrate monitoring (e.g., Prometheus metrics) and alerts (e.g., Slack/email) for failed jobs or system health issues.

requirements.name: Idempotency for Job Processing
requirements.description: Ensure job processing is idempotent to handle duplicate or reprocessed jobs safely.

requirements.name: API for Programmatic Job Control
requirements.description: Provide REST/gRPC APIs to enqueue, inspect, and retry jobs programmatically (e.g., for CI/CD pipelines or other services).

requirements.name: Job Dependencies and Chaining
requirements.description: Support job dependencies (e.g., 'Job B runs after Job A succeeds') and chaining for complex workflows.

requirements.name: Rate Limiting for Job Enqueuing
requirements.description: Implement rate limiting to prevent abuse or accidental flooding of the job queue.
